page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-512GB is an x86_64 cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 shared vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with architectural instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. It lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Paired with this compute allocation is 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 10.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance type contains no bundled local storage, no discrete graphics processors, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid parallel execution with moderate single-core capabilities. The server records a strong PassMark CPU score of 58,184.07, along with strong ratings in extended instructions (77,823.85), encryption (52,934.87), and physics calculations (8,832.01). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches a strong 375.9 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance reflects its 2.0 GHz base frequency, yielding an average Geekbench single-core score of 1294.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating in the bottom 10% (769.08). Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 136.15 GB/sec, while write bandwidth registers at 81.87 GB/sec. In distributed memory benchmarks, the instance delivers 58.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 18,251.77 operations per second in PassMark database operations.

Given its high memory-to-core ratio of over 10:1 alongside shared AMD EPYC cores, the CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-512GB delivers high resource density for scenarios where memory capacity matters more than dedicated per-thread cycles. The lack of integrated local storage means external persistent block storage must be attached for operational persistence. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, caching tiers, parallel data transformations, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency batch processing.
